title: Full certification lifecycle: draft → assigned → under_review → active → expiring_soon → revoked
description: Walks the complete state machine defined in WorkflowTransitionService.getAllowedTransitions for entityType='certification', verifying the mandatory 30-char justification note on approval and that revocation auto-disables Trust Network sharing (DISABLE_SHARING_STATES includes 'revoked').
preconditions: Logged in as org admin with trust_vault.create/approve
A second user (Reviewer) exists in the same org/project
steps: Create a new certification (title, ISO27001:2022 framework, issue/expiry dates, issuing authority) — status starts at 'draft'
Assign Reviewer to the certification — status becomes 'assigned'
As Reviewer, click 'Start Review' — status becomes 'under_review'
As Reviewer, click 'Approve' and attempt to submit with only a 10-character justification note
Retype a 35-character justification note and submit
Enable Trust Network sharing on the now-active certification
Transition the certification to 'expiring_soon' via 'Mark Expiring Soon'
Transition the certification to 'revoked'
Reload the certification detail page and inspect sharingMetadata.trustNetworkEnabled
expectedResult: The 10-character note submission is blocked client-side (counter shows 10/30, button disabled). The 35-character note submission succeeds and status becomes 'active'. After revocation, sharingMetadata.trustNetworkEnabled is automatically false even though it was true moments before — Trust Network partners immediately lose visibility.

title: needs_revision → re_assign → under_review round trip preserves the revision note end to end
description: Verifies transitionNote actually reaches the API and is visible later (regression guard for the previously-silent-discard defect) by round-tripping through a full revision cycle.
steps: As Reviewer, click 'Request Revision' and enter the note 'Issuing authority accreditation number is missing from the uploaded certificate.'
Submit — status becomes 'needs_revision'
As the owner, re-assign the certification back to the same reviewer via 'Re-Assign' — status becomes 're_assign'
As Reviewer, click 'Start Review' — status becomes 'under_review' again
Open the certification's workflow/audit history (GET /certifications/:id/workflow)
expectedResult: The workflow history shows a 'needs_revision' entry whose metadata.note exactly matches the text typed in step 1 — it is not empty, truncated, or replaced with only the targetState.

title: Trust Network sharing toggle is auto-disabled and greyed out the moment a shared certification leaves an active/expiring_soon state
description: TrustNetworkSharingPanel disables the Switch entirely when isActive=false, and WorkflowTransitionService server-side forces sharingMetadata.trustNetworkEnabled=false for any target state outside SHARING_ALLOWED_STATES ({'active','expiring_soon'}). This test verifies both the UI reflects it and the underlying data is actually cleared, not just visually hidden.
preconditions: An active certification has Trust Network sharing enabled with 2 allowed partners
steps: Confirm the Trust Network tab shows 'Sharing enabled' with the Switch checked and interactive
Transition the certification to 'needs_revision'
Re-open the Trust Network tab for this certification
Query the certification directly via GET /certifications/:id and inspect sharingMetadata
expectedResult: The Switch now renders disabled/unchecked and the panel shows the 'only available for Active' warning. The API response confirms sharingMetadata.trustNetworkEnabled is persisted as false server-side (not merely hidden in the UI) — partners lose access immediately, not just visually.

title: Creating a password-protected share link, accessing it, and reviewing the per-access audit trail end to end
description: Covers the full ShareLinkService.create → public access() → getAccessHistory pipeline and the ShareLinkModal 'View access history' / CSV export UI (TV-014 remediation).
preconditions: Logged in as a user with trust_vault.update
steps: Open Share Link modal, set expiry to 7 days, enable password protection with 'MyPass@1234', set recipient email/name
Generate the link and copy the resulting share URL
In a separate incognito/unauthenticated session, open the share URL and enter the correct password
Return to the ShareLinkModal as the authenticated owner and click the chevron to expand 'View access history'
Export the access history as CSV
expectedResult: Public access succeeds after the correct password is entered and accessCount increments to 1. The access history table shows one row with a timestamp, an anonymized IP (last octet zeroed), and no recipient email since none was supplied at access time. The exported CSV contains the same row with proper header quoting.

title: An uncontained incident cannot be shared to Trust Network until its status reaches contained/resolved/closed, and sharing requires a 50-character public summary
description: IncidentForm.jsx SHAREABLE_STATUSES = ['contained','resolved','closed'] gates the sharing Switch, and auto-disables trustNetworkEnabled the moment status is changed back to an unshareable value, per the set() handler's field==='status' branch.
preconditions: Logged in as a user who can create Trust Vault incidents
steps: Open 'Report New Incident', set status to 'open', and attempt to toggle 'Share via Trust Network'
Observe the Switch is disabled with an 'Unavailable' badge and tooltip explaining containment is required
Change status to 'contained' and enable the Trust Network Switch
Attempt to submit with a 20-character publicSummary
Extend publicSummary to 55 characters and submit
Re-open the same incident and change status back to 'investigating'
expectedResult: Sharing cannot be enabled while status='open'. With status='contained', the 20-char summary blocks submission (counter shows red, 20/50) while the 55-char summary submits successfully with trustNetworkEnabled=true. Changing status back to 'investigating' automatically flips trustNetworkEnabled back to false in the form state before the next save.

title: Creating a full-scope and a partial-scope framework mapping on the same certification renders distinct scope badges and control lists
preconditions: At least one compliance framework with 5+ controls is activated for the org
steps: Open the certification's Control Mappings tab and click 'Add Mapping'
Select a framework, choose scope 'Full', and save
Click 'Add Mapping' again, select a different framework, choose scope 'Partial', add exactly 3 controls, and save
Review both mapping cards in the list
expectedResult: The full-scope mapping shows a green 'full' badge with no control count chip. The partial-scope mapping shows an orange 'partial' badge plus a '3 controls' chip, and expanding it lists exactly the 3 selected control codes.

title: Vault Health score and grade improve end to end after adding a second-framework active certification
description: Verifies VaultHealthService.compute is not merely a static display but recomputes from live certification data — computeCertScore awards +20 once distinct_frameworks reaches 2.
preconditions: Org's Trust Vault currently has exactly one active ISO27001 certification and no other frameworks
steps: Record the current Vault Health overall score, grade, and Certifications sub-score
Create and fully approve (draft→active) a second certification under a different framework (e.g. SOC2)
Refresh the Vault Health widget
expectedResult: The Certifications sub-score increases (framework diversity bonus applied) and the overall score/grade updates accordingly on refresh — the widget reflects the new live data rather than a cached or hardcoded value.
